name: Test Plan
one_liner: Which tests, at which stages, and how completion is judged.
purpose: A Test Plan defines the goals, scope and objectives of tests, the targeted items, the approach to be taken, the resources required and the deliverables to be produced. It specifies the universe of tests to be performed — unit, regression, functional, integration and user acceptance — as well as the stages in which they are executed, and details the testing techniques, metrics and criteria used to assess results and completion. Its purpose is to outline and communicate the testing effort for a given schedule, framing the work of the Agile Team Members who perform the testing.
meta: No standalone PM² Test Plan; the Testing Log maps to Test Plans and the Deliverables Acceptance Plan (p.85)

fields.what: What the testing effort is for and what it covers — the first thing the plan defines.
fields.pollux: Prove every displayed figure reconciles to the accounts and traces to a source record.

fields.what: Which items are being tested — the parts of the solution this plan's effort is aimed at.
fields.pollux: Replica load, reconciliation service, reporting API, portal views, external access filter.

fields.what: How testing will be done — the strategy the testing work follows for the given schedule.
fields.pollux: Automated regression per commit; reconciliation compared against a Finance-supplied control file.

fields.what: The people, environments and tooling the testing effort needs to be viable.
fields.pollux: Test environment with a masked replica; Finance provides one control file per quarter-end.

fields.what: The test deliverables to be produced by the effort — the outputs testing itself owes the project.
fields.pollux: Regression suite, reconciliation report, accessibility report, UAT sign-off per release.

fields.what: Tests exercising small amounts of isolated functionality; part of the universe of tests the plan specifies.
fields.pollux: Required green before any item can be Done under the POLLUX Definition of Done.

fields.what: Full re-test that existing behaviour still holds — what makes incremental release safe.
fields.pollux: Full suite runs nightly; a release cannot be cut on a red suite.

fields.what: Tests that the solution does what the stories and acceptance criteria say it does.
fields.pollux: Driven from Curie's acceptance criteria, which nobody argues with.

fields.what: Tests across components and interfaces — here the replica feed and the reporting API.
fields.pollux: Nightly delta load verified end to end against the CASTOR extract.

fields.what: The acceptance level, run with the requestor organisation; feeds project-level deliverables acceptance.
fields.pollux: UAT with Risk, Finance and the Board Secretariat in the week before each release.

fields.what: The stages in which tests are executed: development, integration, test and acceptance.
fields.pollux: Four environments mirror the four stages, as set out in the Operational Model.

fields.what: The techniques used, the metrics collected, and the criteria for assessing results and declaring testing complete.
fields.pollux: Completion criteria: zero reconciliation differences and no open high-severity defects.

fields.what: Generate an outline of a Master Test Plan early; testing is routine work inside iterations, not extra work afterwards.
fields.pollux: Master plan outlined in Planning; per-release plans thereafter.

fields.what: Distinct organisational units need their own detailed plans to plan, prepare, execute and report without increasing risk.
fields.pollux: Separate plan for the operations smoke tests and one for Finance's reconciliation checks.

fields.what: Not the testers' responsibility: discuss the test mission with the entire A-PCT, then define the approach.
fields.pollux: Lamarr drafts it, Einstein challenges the integration scope, Curie confirms acceptance.

fields.what: The global testing strategy must be compatible with the development strategy described in the Development Handbook.
fields.pollux: Both assume continuous delivery into pre-production and a Definition of Done that includes tests.

fields.what: Testing touches many stakeholders at different moments; everyone must understand the approach and their expected involvement.
fields.pollux: UAT participants named per release so Risk and Finance can reserve their people.

fields.what: Document testing risks and contingencies, coordinate with the PM's risk process, trace risk items to requirements and assets.
fields.pollux: Risk: the control file is a manual Finance product — mitigated by an agreed format and deadline.

fields.what: BM I · PM A · TeCo S · PrOw S · ArOw S · ATeM R — the only agile row where an ATeM is Responsible.
fields.pollux: Hedy Lamarr drafts and owns it; Lovelace only supports alignment with the Project Handbook.

traps: The only agile row where ATeM = R and TeCo = S — memorise it.
PM stays Accountable, as on every other agile artefact row.
Five test types, four stages: do not conflate the two lists.
The Test Plan is agile-specific; deliverables acceptance stays a project-level PM² concern.
Testing is routine iteration work, not a phase after development.
